meta.title: 微软面试为什么考井盖｜博弈论
meta.title_en: The Game Theory Behind Microsoft's Manhole Question

scenes.title_cn: 一道答案尽人皆知的面试题
scenes.title_en: An interview question everyone already knows
scenes.context: 抛出问题：微软十几年还在考「窨井盖为什么是圆的」，答案网上随手就能搜到，那为什么还考？由此引入博弈论：互相预判、后手背后还有后手。
sentences: 为什么微软在十几年后，依然用这道题来面试工程师？
Why does Microsoft still use this question to interview engineers, even after all these years?
十几年后依然：still ... even after all these years
答案你肯定知道，网上随便一搜就有。
You surely know the answer — a quick search online is all it takes.
随便一搜就有：a quick search is all it takes
博弈论就是互相预判：后手背后还有后手，以此类推。
Game theory is all about anticipation: there's a countermove behind every countermove, and so on.
后手背后还有后手：a countermove behind every countermove
paraphrase: 答案在网上 → 题目岂不是没意义
If the answer is online, the question seems pointless.
互相预判 → 层层留后手
Players anticipate each other, one level deeper each time.
scenes.speak: Why does Microsoft still use this question to interview engineers, even after all these years? You surely know the answer — a quick search online is all it takes. Game theory is all about anticipation: there's a countermove behind every countermove, and so on.

scenes.title_en: The hidden play is integrity: the yellow-card test
scenes.context: 揭秘微软的后手是「诚信」：面试官先说知道答案就如实说、直接跳过；若答「方的容易掉下去」就亮出黄牌，再追问一句「还有吗」来确认。
sentences: 那微软这道题的「后手」是什么？是诚信。
So what's the hidden play in Microsoft's question? Integrity.
后手：hidden play / countermove
面试前，面试官会先说：如果你知道答案，请如实告诉我，我们直接跳过看下一题。
Before the interview, the interviewer says up front: if you already know the answer, be honest and tell me — we'll just move on to the next question.
如实告诉我：be honest and tell me
你要是想都没想就答「方的容易掉下去」，面试官就对你的诚信亮出黄牌，再问一句：「还有吗？」
If you blurt out 'square ones fall in' without a second thought, the interviewer flags your integrity and simply asks: 'Anything else?'
亮出黄牌：flag your integrity
paraphrase: A yellow card means doubt has been raised.
再问一句 → 一锤定音
One more question settles the judgment.
scenes.speak: So what's the hidden play in Microsoft's question? Integrity. Before the interview, the interviewer says up front: if you already know the answer, be honest and tell me — we'll just move on to the next question. If you blurt out 'square ones fall in' without a second thought, the interviewer flags your integrity and simply asks: 'Anything else?'

scenes.context: 只背过网上答案的人当场懵掉：工程学上还有别的解释——圆盖只需一个半径尺寸，方盖有长宽两个尺寸，挖圆洞也更简单。这道题有三层含义。
sentences: 只背过网上那一条答案的面试者，这时就懵了。
Candidates who only memorized the single online answer are instantly stumped.
当场懵掉：instantly stumped
工程学上还有别的解释：圆盖只要一个半径尺寸，方盖却有长和宽两个尺寸。
Engineering offers other explanations: a round cover has just one radius, while a square one has two dimensions — length and width.
半径尺寸：a single radius
所以这道题有三层含义：考诚信、考多角度思考、也考你够不够格当微软的工程师。
So the question has three layers: it tests integrity, it tests multi-angle thinking, and it tests whether you're the engineer Microsoft wants.
三层含义：three layers
paraphrase: 背答案 → 经不起追问
Memorized answers can't survive follow-up questions.
一个角度 → 多角度论证
One angle gives way to multi-angle reasoning.
scenes.speak: Candidates who only memorized the single online answer are instantly stumped. That's because engineering offers other explanations: a round cover has just one radius, while a square one has two dimensions — length and width. So the question has three layers: it tests integrity, it tests multi-angle thinking, and it tests whether you're the engineer Microsoft wants.

scenes.title_en: A twist ending: the guy who said 'square'
scenes.context: 微软的朋友说真有人坚持方盖比圆盖好、还讲得有理有据，结果被录用还送去了销售部。好面试题内嵌博弈论：看着考A，其实考B。
sentences: 我微软的朋友告诉我，还真有人坚持说方盖比圆盖好，而且讲得有理有据。
A friend at Microsoft told me that someone actually insisted square covers are better — and he argued it with real substance.
有理有据：with real substance
后来这哥们居然被录用了，还被送去了销售部门。
That guy actually got hired in the end — and sent straight to the sales department.
居然被录用：actually got hired
好的面试题就应该是这样：内嵌博弈论，看起来是考A，其实是考B。
A good interview question works like this: game theory is built in — it looks like it's testing A, but it's really testing B.
内嵌博弈论：game theory built in
paraphrase: 反对标准答案 → 照样被录用
Going against the expected answer can still win you the job.
表面考知识 → 实际考人性
The surface tests knowledge, but the real target is character.
scenes.speak: Here's the twist: a friend at Microsoft told me that someone actually insisted square covers are better — and he argued it with real substance. That guy actually got hired in the end, and sent straight to the sales department. A good interview question works like this: game theory is built in — it looks like it's testing A, but it's really testing B.

practice: The answer is all over the internet.
He blurted out an answer without a second thought.
He argued his case with real substance.
pitfalls: ✕ 直译腔：The answer, a search online casually will have it.
✓ 地道说法：A quick search online is all it takes.
「随便一搜就有」别逐字直译，用 it's all it takes / it's right there 更自然。
✕ 直译腔：The interviewer showed a yellow card to his integrity.
✓ 地道说法：The interviewer flagged his integrity.
「亮黄牌」是中文比喻，英文用 flag / call into question，直译 yellow card 反而出戏。
✕ 直译腔：The round cover only has one radius size.
✓ 地道说法：A round cover has just a single radius.
「半径尺寸」直接说 radius 就好，不必再加 size。
✕ 直译腔：This is a true thing.
✓ 地道说法：This actually happened / I'm not making this up.
「这是真事情」口语里常说 it actually happened，不要逐字说 a true thing。
shifts: 以为面试题考的是知识点
发现它考的是「你是什么样的人」
以为背熟标准答案就稳了
发现经得起追问的思考才值钱
以为题目只有唯一正确答案
发现论证充分的反面观点也有价值
